content.value_statement: Mobile teams need safe ways to change app behavior without shipping a new build. This skill guides Remote Config setup, defaults, template edits, and reviewed CLI deployments.
actual_capabilities: Explains Android and iOS setup prerequisites for Firebase Remote Config.
Shows where to add Remote Config and Analytics SDK dependencies.
Guides default values for Android XML and iOS property list files.
Describes Firebase CLI steps to get, deploy, and verify templates.
Requires user review before deploying Remote Config changes.
limitations: Requires an existing Firebase project or help from a Firebase project setup skill.
Requires Firebase CLI access and valid user credentials for live template operations.
Does not judge business impact, rollout safety, or experiment design alone.
SDK version examples may need updates for strict dependency policies.

use_cases.title: Add Remote Config to a mobile app
use_cases.description: Set up dependencies, defaults, and basic fetch behavior for a new Android or iOS integration.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature flag rollout
use_cases.description: Create or update parameters, define targeting logic, and review the local template before deployment.

use_cases.title: Audit Remote Config operations
use_cases.description: Fetch the current template, inspect planned changes, and verify version history after deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start Android Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Firebase Remote Config to my Android app. List the required project files, dependencies, and default value steps.

prompt_templates.title: Start iOS Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through Firebase Remote Config setup for my iOS app. Include package dependencies, initialization, and default values.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me fetch my Firebase Remote Config template, add a reviewed feature flag, and prepare it for deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Remote Config rollout plan. Check targeting, defaults, deployment readiness, and post-deploy verification steps.

output_examples.input: Help me add Remote Config to my Android app.
output_examples.output: The skill would identify required Firebase files, recommend Gradle dependency changes, define default values, and explain fetch and activate behavior.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Remote Config feature flag for review.
output_examples.output: The skill would fetch the current template, describe the planned parameter and condition changes, then ask for review before deployment.

output_examples.input: Check whether my rollout process is safe.
output_examples.output: The skill would confirm defaults, project targeting, human review, deployment scope, and version history verification.

best_practices: Confirm the Firebase project ID before running CLI commands.
Define in-app defaults for every Remote Config parameter.
Review template changes before any deployment command.
anti_patterns: Deploying Remote Config changes without human review.
Using Remote Config values before safe defaults are available.
Mixing unrelated feature behavior into one parameter.

faq.question: Does this skill create Firebase projects?
faq.answer: It explains prerequisites and points to project setup guidance. It focuses on Remote Config setup and template management.

faq.question: Can it deploy Remote Config changes?
faq.answer: It can guide Firebase CLI deployment, but it requires user review before making changes live.

faq.question: Does it support Android and iOS?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes setup references for Android Gradle projects and iOS Swift Package Manager projects.

faq.question: Does it include feature flag guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers parameters, conditions, template edits, and safe rollout review steps.

faq.question: Does it replace Firebase console review?
faq.answer: No. Use Firebase console or CLI review for sensitive releases and production changes.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: Firebase CLI actions require a logged-in account with access to the target Firebase project.
